I am an old woman, eighty years now, and this small piece of land behind my house is where I plant my yam and cocoyam with some cassava mixed in. I do what my mother taught me and what I have done every year — I put the ash from my kitchen fire and the droppings from the goats around the mounds, I keep the seed yam from last harvest, and I weed with my own hands when my grandchildren help me. I have no money for the fertilizer they sell in town, and my legs cannot carry me to the agro-dealer anyway; the rain here is plenty so I do not need to fetch water for my crops. My plot is very small, just behind the compound, so I manage it myself with help from the children when they come from school.
